questions.q: Which part of an electric drive adapts the supply to what the motor needs?
questions.explain: The power modulator (converter) changes voltage, current and frequency to suit the motor.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT an advantage of electric drives?
options: Available in a wide range of power ratings
Can be started and loaded quickly
Can hold a load with zero electrical braking torque
questions.explain: Electrical braking cannot produce a holding torque; a mechanical brake is needed for that.

questions.q: A single motor driving several machines through a line shaft is a:
questions.explain: In a group drive one motor drives a shaft that feeds several machines through belts and pulleys.

questions.q: Which drive is typical of rolling mills and paper machines, where each part of one machine has its own motor?
questions.explain: Multi-motor drives give each mechanism of a complex machine its own motor.

questions.q: The torque of a loaded hoist (lifting a weight) is:
questions.explain: Gravity gives an active load torque that keeps its direction even when the motion reverses.

questions.q: For a fan or centrifugal pump the load torque varies roughly as:
questions.explain: Fan and pump loads follow $T \propto n^2$, so $k = 2$ in $T = C\,T_r (n/n_r)^k$.

questions.q: A machine tool in a lathe needing constant power has load torque that varies as:
questions.explain: Constant power means $T\omega$ is constant, so $T \propto 1/n$ ($k = -1$).

questions.q: Which motor has the steepest fall of speed with torque, making it ideal for traction?
questions.explain: For a DC series motor $T \propto I^2$ and $n \propto 1/I$, so $n \propto 1/\sqrt{T}$.

questions.q: A synchronous motor's speed–torque characteristic is:
options: A horizontal line up to pull-out torque
questions.explain: Speed stays at synchronous speed until the load exceeds the pull-out torque.

questions.q: The operating point of a drive is stable if, near equilibrium:
questions.explain: A small speed rise must make load torque exceed motor torque, so the drive slows back down.

questions.q: Positive speed with negative (braking) torque is quadrant:
questions.explain: Quadrant II is forward braking: the machine generates while turning forward.

questions.q: A hoist lowering a heavy load, with the motor holding it back, works in quadrant:
questions.explain: Speed is reversed (down) while motor torque still acts upward: reverse braking, quadrant IV.

questions.q: Which braking method reverses the supply to the armature and wastes the most energy?
questions.explain: Plugging dissipates both the kinetic energy and power drawn from the supply in the resistance.

questions.q: Regenerative braking of a DC motor occurs when:
questions.explain: When the back EMF exceeds the supply voltage, current reverses and power flows back to the supply.

questions.q: In dynamic braking the armature is:
options: Disconnected and switched across a resistor
questions.explain: The kinetic energy is dissipated as heat in the braking resistor.

questions.q: A motor's temperature rise reaches about 63.2% of its final value after:
questions.explain: $\theta = \theta_{ss}(1 - e^{-t/\tau})$, and at $t = \tau$ this is $1 - e^{-1} = 0.632$.

questions.q: The heating time constant is $\tau = C/D$. For the cooling time constant of a self-ventilated motor at standstill:
options: It is shorter than the heating constant
It is longer, because ventilation is poorer
questions.explain: At standstill a self-cooled motor loses its fan airflow, so $D$ falls and the cooling time constant is longer.

questions.q: The equivalent current method sizes a motor for a varying load using:
options: The rms current over the cycle
questions.explain: Copper losses depend on $I^2$, so the rms current gives the same heating.

questions.q: Why is a flywheel fitted to a pulsating load such as a press?
options: To smooth the power taken from the supply
questions.explain: The flywheel stores energy at light load and gives it back at peak load, so the motor and supply see a smoother demand.

questions.q: In a single-phase fully controlled rectifier with continuous conduction, the average output voltage is:
questions.explain: For a full converter $V_a = \frac{2V_m}{\pi}\cos\alpha$; it goes negative for $\alpha > 90°$, which allows regeneration.

questions.q: A fully controlled converter can work in which quadrants on its own?
questions.explain: Current cannot reverse, but voltage can, so it works in quadrants I and IV. A dual converter is needed for all four.

questions.q: Below base speed, V/f control keeps what constant?
questions.explain: Keeping $V/f$ constant keeps the flux, and so the maximum torque, roughly constant.

questions.q: Adding resistance to the rotor of a slip-ring induction motor:
options: Moves maximum torque to a higher slip, raising starting torque
questions.explain: $s_{max} \propto R_2$, while the maximum torque itself stays the same.

questions.q: What is the synchronous speed of a 6-pole, 50 Hz induction motor in rpm?
A 4-pole, 50 Hz induction motor runs at 1425 rpm. What is its slip? Give a decimal.
The rotor input power is 10 kW at slip 0.04. What is the rotor copper loss in watts?
questions.explain: Rotor copper loss $= s\,P_g = 0.04 \times 10\,000 = 400$ W.

questions.q: A motor has $\theta_{ss} = 60$ °C and $\tau = 60$ min. Starting cold, what is its temperature rise after 60 min, in °C?
A DC shunt motor on 220 V has $R_a = 0.5\ \Omega$ and runs with $E_b = 210$ V. What is the armature current in A?
A single-phase full converter has $V_m = 325$ V and $\alpha = 60°$. What is the average armature voltage in volts?
In continuous conduction, the output of a buck converter with duty cycle $\delta$ is:
questions.explain: Equal inductor current rise and fall give $(E-V_c)\delta = V_c(1-\delta)$, so $V_c = \delta E$.

questions.q: Which converter gives an inverted output that can be above or below the input?
questions.explain: For a buck-boost, $|V_o| = \delta E/(1-\delta)$ with reversed polarity.

questions.q: Discontinuous conduction in a chopper means:
options: The inductor current is zero for part of each cycle
questions.explain: In DCM the inductor current falls to zero before the next switching period starts.

questions.q: A buck converter has $R = 1.44\ \Omega$, $\delta = 0.6$ and $f = 10$ kHz. What is the critical inductance in µH?
A boost converter steps 40 V up to 150 V. What is the duty cycle? Give a decimal.
A buck-boost converter gives 50 V from a 35 V source. What is the duty cycle? Give a decimal.
Star–delta starting reduces the starting line current to what fraction of its DOL value?
questions.explain: Each phase gets $V_L/\sqrt3$ and the star connection reduces line current again by $\sqrt3$, giving one third.

questions.q: Why is a starter used with a 3-phase induction motor?
options: The motor cannot start on its own
To reduce starting current and give overload protection
questions.explain: A 3-phase IM is self-starting; the starter limits current and protects the motor.

questions.q: An auto-transformer starter uses a 60% tapping on a motor whose DOL starting current is 300 A. What is the starting line current in A?
questions.explain: Line current $= x^2 I_{sc} = 0.36 \times 300 = 108$ A.

questions.q: $I_{sc} = 5I_{FL}$, $s_{FL} = 0.05$, and a stator resistance starter applies 60% voltage. What is $T_{st}/T_{FL}$?
Why can't a DC series motor regenerate into the supply?
options: Its armature resistance is too high
Reversed current also reverses the series field, so the EMF cannot be maintained
questions.explain: The series field reverses with the current and weakens the flux.

questions.q: A drive where a manual command starts a preset automatic sequence (start, brake, reverse) uses:
questions.explain: Semi-automatic control pairs a manual command device with an automatic device that runs a preset sequence.

questions.q: A motor has constant loss 400 W and full-load copper loss 800 W. What are its total losses at half load, in W?
Why does a single-phase induction motor not self-start?
options: Its rotor resistance is too high
Its stator field pulsates instead of rotating, giving zero net starting torque
Its slip is zero at standstill
questions.explain: A single winding produces a pulsating field, which gives zero net torque at standstill.
